prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: ফসল মৌসুমভিত্তিক বপন, কর্তন ও ফলন সূচি (language bn).
Grid: 5 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ফসল" · longest unbreakable word 69px · one-line width 149px
  col 2: header "বপন" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 263px
  col 3: header "কাটা" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 239px
  col 4: header "ফলন (টন/হেক্টর)" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 108px
  col 5: header "মন্তব্য" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 1035px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A crop-by-crop season reference: compare when each crop is sown and harvested, what it yields, and any notes.","reading":"Primarily row-wise: fix the crop in col 1, read cols 2–3 as one sowing-to-harvest window, then col 4 yield and col 5 caveat; secondarily scan down the date columns to compare seasons.","groups":["col 1 is the row anchor","cols 2–3 are a paired timing unit and must stay adjacent","col 4 is the quantitative outcome","col 5 is free-text commentary attached to the whole row"],"keep_intact":["crop names in col 1","month/season names and date ranges in cols 2–3","yield numbers and the টন/হেক্টর unit in col 4","row identity"],"may_wrap":["date ranges at spaces and em dashes","the yield header between ফলন and (টন/হেক্টর)","parenthetical crop qualifiers","comments in col 5, which must wrap extensively"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [90, 67, 65, 63, 74] · table 360×3301px · row heights [83, 594, 455, 525, 571, 501, 571] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 25 lines · mid-word splits 29
Design r0B: widths [90, 87, 89, 63, 170] · table 500×1138px · row heights [83, 199, 153, 176, 176, 176, 176] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0 · OVERFLOWS the box by 140px
Design r0C: widths [90, 66, 64, 63, 130] · table 414×1557px · row heights [83, 292, 222, 222, 222, 246, 269] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 12 lines · mid-word splits 20 · OVERFLOWS the box by 54px

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r0A","good":"Fits the 360px box exactly, so nothing is cut off; the header row is legible and the crop names still sit in a clear first column.","problems":"Catastrophic vertical stretch (3301px tall, single rows up to 594px / 25 lines) and 29 mid-word splits. Every cell is a narrow stack of fragments: 'বোরো ধান (উফশী)' breaks into four lines, the sowing window into 'ডিসেম্ব/র শেষ/সপ্তাহ—/জানুয়ারি/র মাঝা/মাঝি', and even the short yield range '৫.৮–৬.৮' is broken. Because cols 2 and 3 are stacked, the sowing→harvest pair can no longer be read as one span, which is the table's whole point.","cause":"Widths 67/65/63/74 leave only 46/44/42/53px of text room — below the 66–68px longest words in cols 2, 3 and 5 — so the browser is forced to break inside words everywhere. Col 5's 74px also sets the row height for the entire table."},{"design":"r0B","good":"Zero mid-word splits; crop names, month names and the '৫.৮–৬.৮' style ranges all stay intact. Rows are compact (176px) and read as units, the header block is clean, and the table is only 1138px tall — by far the most usable of the three.","problems":"Overflows the box by 140px, so the মন্তব্য column is sliced off at the right edge — the commentary, which is the reason the rows are tall, is the part you can't see. Col 5 will be tall (~15 lines), so this is the zero-split floor, not the final answer."},{"name":"balanced-440","widths":[90,87,89,63,111],"change":"Keeps the same no-split floors for cols 1–4 and spends the extra 22px on col 5 (99px of text), which still fits every unbreakable word in the comments but cuts roughly 3 lines per row versus the tight version. 81px overflow, rows around 220px, table near 1500px — the best height/scroll compromise."},{"name":"comment-first","widths":[90,88,90,63,140],"change":"Refines r0B rather than squeezing: trim col 5 from 170 to 140 and give cols 2–3 two extra px each, dropping the overflow from 140 to 112px while keeping zero splits. Col 5 at 119px of text runs about 9 lines and rows stay near 180px, so this is the option to choose if the commentary is the main thing readers come for and a right-edge scroll is acceptable."}]}
